summary: Iter45: Tested the merged CalendarView and the reschedule backend (new_date, past-date checks), Pi sandbox payments, CORS from FRONTEND_URL, worker read-only view and CSV export. Backend: 14/16 pytest pass. The 2 failures are a missing role check (a worker can reschedule through the API) and a 500 on an invalid ObjectId. Frontend: everything requested works. The admin calendar loads with 8 worker columns, the mini month calendar and the Mreža/Arhiva tabs. Dragging a block to a grid slot opens the reschedule modal with date and time dropdown; confirming persists the move (verified via API: 12:30, is_rescheduled=true). Dropping on a future mini-calendar day opens the modal with that date and moves the reservation (26.10 -> 28.10 14:00), and the view follows to the target day. Dropping on a past mini-calendar day shows the toast 'Nije moguće premestiti rezervaciju u prošlost.' and no modal opens. 'Nova Rezervacija' on a past day shows the toast 'Nije moguće kreirati rezervaciju u prošlosti.' and no modal opens. In the worker view (Marija) blocks have draggable=false, clicking opens no dialog, and there are no tabs or new-reservation button. CSV export downloads rezervacije_2026-10-28.csv, but only for super_admin; it has been super_admin-only in all git history.

critical.issue: No role check. A worker token (worker@salon.com) can reschedule any reservation in the tenant (200 OK, including other workers' reservations). The UI hides drag for workers but the API does not enforce it. Add a check: role in (admin, super_admin) else 403, plus check_tenant_access.

Security: is_sandbox comes from the client and needs no auth. Anyone can POST {booking_id, paymentId, is_sandbox:true} with X-Tenant-ID and mark any reservation payment_status=confirmed. The sandbox branch should be gated by a server-side env flag (e.g. PI_SANDBOX=true), not by the request body.

minor.issue: An invalid reservation_id or new_worker_id (not an ObjectId) returns 500 (bson InvalidId). It should return 400 or 404.
Cancelled reservations can be rescheduled: the find_one does not filter on status. The move is also not validated against the worker's work hours or day off on the new_date.
background_tasks defaults to None. It is injected by FastAPI so it works, but the default is misleading.

ui_bugs.issue: onDragLeave on every cell calls handleDragEnd, which clears dragData and dropTarget as soon as the cursor leaves the first cell. Effects: the drop highlight and the 'Spustite rezervaciju na željeni datum' hint vanish mid-drag, and handleDragOver returns early (dragData null), so dropEffect is not set. Drop still works only thanks to the dataTransfer fallback. onDragLeave should only clear dropTarget.

issues: The date header and mini-calendar month use the Cyrillic date-fns 'sr' locale ('петак, 23. октобар 2026', 'октобар 2026') while the rest of the UI is in Latin script. Use the srLatn locale.
Missing diacritics in toasts on CalendarView.jsx lines 278/284: 'Nije moguce' should be 'Nije moguće'.
The reschedule modal uses a native <select> for time instead of the shadcn Select. For a mini-calendar drop the worker cannot be changed, and 'STARO' shows selectedDate rather than res.date.

action_items: Add a role check (admin/super_admin only) to PUT /api/reservations/{id}/reschedule
Gate the Pi sandbox payment path with a server env flag instead of client-provided is_sandbox
Wrap ObjectId() parsing in reschedule and return 400/404 instead of 500
Fix onDragLeave in CalendarView grid cells so it does not clear dragData
Use the srLatn locale for date headers; fix 'moguce' -> 'moguće'
critical_code_review_comments: CalendarView.jsx is 836 lines (>700). Split out the reschedule modal, mini calendar and grid.
handleDrop and handleDateDrop duplicate the drag-data fallback and the past-date validation blocks. Extract them into a helper.

Frontend 'today' checks use browser local time while the backend uses the salon timezone (Europe/Belgrade). This can mismatch for users in other timezones; the backend is authoritative so it is safe, but the UX could be confusing.
